question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code to review every pull request. Developers complain that the review comments mix real defects with remarks about variable naming, formatting, and patterns that the team uses on purpose in its own modules. The current prompt asks Claude to review the code and report any problems it finds. Which change to the review prompt will most effectively improve the precision of the review comments?

options.text: List the issue categories to report, such as logic bugs and security flaws, and the categories to skip, such as minor style and local conventions.
options.reason: The guide recommends specific review criteria that define which issues to report (bugs, security) and which to skip (minor style, local patterns), instead of confidence-based filtering.

options.text: Ask Claude to assign a confidence score to each finding and post only the findings above a fixed threshold to the pull request.
options.reason: This relies on confidence-based filtering, which the guide says to replace with specific criteria that define which issue categories to report and which to skip.

options.text: Instruct Claude to be conservative and report only high-confidence findings, so that uncertain remarks about style are dropped from the review output.
options.reason: The guide states that general instructions like "be conservative" or "only report high-confidence findings" fail to improve precision compared to specific categorical criteria.

options.text: Add an instruction telling Claude to be thorough and to make sure that every comment it posts is accurate and genuinely important to the team.
options.reason: This is a vague instruction; the guide stresses that explicit criteria work better than vague instructions for improving precision and reducing false positives.
